behavior.name: Haas's basic program O40001 (2023 Mill Operator's Manual, p. 102), on the VF-3
behavior.description: Haas's example as printed, on the VF-3 twin: tool 1, a rapid to the part's top right corner, the spindle at 1000 rpm, a feed 0.1 in down at 20 in/min, a straight cut to X-4. Y-4., and back to Z and Y home. The stock stands on the trunnion's platter, the path centred on it; A and B stay home (decisions 0035 and 0036). Every code it uses has the same meaning in the 2012 Classic manual.

why: Directions of X, Y and Z as on the TM-1 (decision 0035): +X the tool to the operator's right, the twin's +y; +Y the tool towards the back, the twin's -x; +Z up. The VF-3 twin has the same frame (+x the front, +y the machine's own left).

Home: Z at the top of its travel; Y at its + end (the table towards the operator) [INFERENCE, as the TM-1]; X at its + end, the table at its operator-left end: a STAND-IN, as on the TM-1 (decision 0035).

A turns about Haas's +X, B about the platter's normal; their + is the tool's motion by the right hand rule, and the trunnion's joints turn the other way ("the fingers will point opposite of the positive rotary table movement", the 2011 rotary manual, p. 34). +A follows that rule with the manual's caveat ("Different table movements are possible ... depending on the equipment, parameter settings", p. 35); +B about the platter's normal is a STAND-IN [INFERENCE]: the manual's B turns about Y, a tilting rotary's other layout (decision 0036). The lab's jog of +A and +B settles both (the visit list, item 10).
Home of A and B: the joints' 0, the cradle level as photographed (133938) and B as built: a STAND-IN; the tool changer is left out of the twin, so M06 stops the spindle and raises Z only.
The work part is the platter: the trunnion stands on the table's middle, so the stock and the drawn path ride the platter (decision 0036).
Tool T1: 3.0 in from the spindle nose's face to its tip, a STAND-IN (as on the TM-1); its length offset H01 is touched off on the twin, on the top of the stock.
Stock: a 2.0 in block on the platter, a STAND-IN; Z0 is its top, as the program's comment says.

Work offset G54: the platter's centre is under the spindle at the twin's 0, machine X -20, Y -10 in (measured on haas/vf3@v1); the path, X 0 to -4 and Y 0 to -4, is centred on it: G54 X -18, Y -8. A STAND-IN: an operator's set-up.
Setting 9 (units): inch, a STAND-IN; the program is written in inches.
